dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Hmm, what's wrong with this tea?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Is it just that the soil here has lost its fertility? Or has the weather just not been favorable? Either way, the tea doesn't have the same flavor as the previous harvests.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: And since the problem lies with the tea, no amount of additional processing will help. We have to serve it to the adeptus soon. Ohh, what shall we do?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: ...And those visiting guests and merchants. How will we deal with them?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Alright, I have to get to work, too. What's that boy Jin doing now, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you tried adding fertilizer?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Yes, among other things. We've fertilized the soil, tried water from a different source, and we've even had people stationed by the field on rotation, but nothing's helped.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: If nothing's done, we're not going to have any tea this year.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: With good water and soil, we're going to have great tea going forward, period.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Greetings, Uncle Luo.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: What brings you here? Are you here for a spot of tea? Come sit, I'll brew some for you.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Thanks to you, the tea business here in our village is booming. If we had waited another year, I don't know what would have happened.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Sure. I have to go down to the field in a bit, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the tea leaves...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: The issue with the water and the soil has been resolved thanks to you and the adeptus. But the tea... The new harvest needs time, so we'll just have to give the re-baked aged tea to the merchants.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Moreover, variations in the water and the soil have a huge impact. I mean, even a little bit of extra rain can bring the quality of the tea down.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: With such drastic changes, there's no guarantee that we'll grow great tea going forward, adeptus's help or not.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's re-baked aged tea?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Some tea leaves taste better when they're newly harvested, and some when they've been sitting in storage for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Some leaves must be stored for years and re-baked from time to time.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: They're difficult to make, and even harder to store. But if those two hurdles are overcome, the flavor is... What's the right word for it... Ah, yes, "peerless"! Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: ...It's a shame that people these days don't want to wait, nor do they want to learn.
